title: Primed benchmark runbook and capture guidelines
body:
Purpose
This runbook documents a pragmatic throughput benchmarking harness and telemetry-capture guidelines optimized for repeatability and variance reduction. It's intended for team members running medium-to-large scale experiments (1–1000 client threads / up to 20k rps) against the serving runtime to validate throughput SLOs and uncover bottlenecks.

Goals
- Produce repeatable throughput numbers across runs and hosts (±3% target for stable workloads).
- Provide clear warmup/priming strategy so cache-sensitive models and JIT/compilation effects are stable.
- Capture rich telemetry so root-cause analysis is quick (latency tails, GPU kernels, scheduler queues, OS-level stats).
- Standardize artifact naming and run metadata to ease change comparisons and automated regression detection.

When to use this runbook
- New model variants being onboarded for production serving.
- Kernel / compiler / runtime config changes that might affect per-token throughput.
- Cost/latency tradeoff experiments (batch size, quantization, kv-cache policies).
- Pre-release validation of Dedicated capacity profiles.

Quick checklist (run before every official measurement)
- [ ] Use a clean machine snapshot (no unrelated cron jobs or background experiments).
- [ ] Sync clock and NTP; note timezone and epoch.
- [ ] Ensure GPU drivers + cuDNN + runtime binaries versioned and recorded.
- [ ] Clear disk/iocaches and restart relevant daemons if possible.
- [ ] Reserve network path and isolate clients from noisy neighbors.
- [ ] Set RNG seeds for client-side workload generators and note them in metadata.

Environment and config conventions
- Always capture and commit the following as run metadata: git commit of bench harness, docker image sha for serving host, kernel and driver versions, model filename + quantization profile, and exact loadgen config (attached below).
- Use the dedicated loadgen namespace for benchmark traffic, avoid mixing with real traffic.
- Pin host to single NIC and capture tc/netem rules if any interference is expected.

Warmup / priming strategy (multi-layered)
We observed many transient throughput artifacts come from three sources: first-request penalties (JITs, kernel selection), KV-cache cold misses, and memory/allocator warmups. The warmup protocol below layers short, targeted priming before long runs: 
1) micro-priming (30–60s): 1–4 short single-inference requests at high concurrency to trigger JITs and initial allocation. Purpose: compile kernels, warm thread-local allocators.
2) cache-priming (2–4 min): run mini-benchmark using representative prefix distribution to populate KV caches and tokenizers. Purpose: reduce initial token variance on models with heavy KV reuse.
3) ramp-to-plateau (10–20 min): gradually increase offered load in stages (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) holding each for 1–3 min to let autoscalers and batching equilibrium settle.
4) steady window (15–30 min): record final measurement window once metrics show stable drift under threshold.

Detecting stability programmatically
- Sample p50/p95/p99 latency every 10s and compute windowed coefficient of variation (CV) over the last N samples (N=30 by default).
- Stability condition: p95 CV < 0.02 and throughput CV < 0.03 for three consecutive windows => mark run stable.
- If not stable after maximal duration (60m), abort and record failure mode.

Load generator config (example JSON snippet)
{"name": "mixed-short-long-primed", "concurrency": 128, "ramp": [{"pct":10, "dur_s":60}, {"pct":30, "dur_s":120}, {"pct":60, "dur_s":300}, {"pct":100, "dur_s":900}], "rng_seed": 1729, "workload_mix": [{"type":"short", "seq_len":16, "weight":0.7}, {"type":"long", "seq_len":512, "weight":0.3}], "prefix_variation": "sampled_from_corpus", "priming": {"micro_s":45, "cache_min_s":180}}
Note: embed this exact blob in run metadata so downstream analysis has deterministic inputs.

RNG and seed hygiene
- Two separate seeds: client message sampling seed and loadgen schedule seed. Both must be recorded.
- Never reuse the same seed across platform experiments intended to compare with production data — instead, commit a seed map and reuse only for strictly reproducible debugging runs.

Telemetry to capture (minimum)
- Loadgen: offered qps, success/failure counts, client-side latency histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99), request serialization times.
- Server: per-worker token throughput, batching distribution (batch sizes and frequency), queue depth, in-flight requests.
- HW: GPU utilization (SM%, mem%), GPU power draw, PCIe bandwidth, CPU steal/irq, memory allocator metrics.
- OS/Network: NIC tx/rx rates, retransmits, socket queue lengths, ioctl/block metrics.
- Runtime internals: kernel selection events, fused-kernel fallback counts, quant-dequant conversion counts, KV cache hit/miss by prefix length.
- Tracing: sample 1 in 200 requests for full flamegraph/tracer capture to keep cost manageable.

Artifact naming and metadata convention
- Use: bench/<model>-<profile>-<concurrency>-<seed>-<date>.tar.gz
- Inside artifact: loadgen-config.json, server-metadata.json, perf-raw.csv (10s cadence rows), trace-samples/ (n=8), run-notes.txt.

Post-run validation and expected pass criteria
- Throughput does not drop below 95% of median observed in the steady window.
- p99 latency below target SLO (configured per-model).
- Batch-size distribution matches expected operating point (no pathological 1-token batch storm).
- No sustained GPU saturation with 100% synthetic busy loop (indicates constrained host).
- If any metric fails, annotate root-cause hypotheses in run-notes and attach traces.

Common failure modes and mitigations
- High tail with low average: usually memory pressure or periodic GC. Mitigation: increase malloc pool, use hugepages, check CPU frequency governors.
- Throughput oscillation: typically due to autoscaler/queue interplay. Mitigation: add longer ramp stage or pin worker counts.
- Warmup regressions between runs: confirm image sha / driver version; rerun micro-priming and compare JIT logs.
- Batch flattening (too many small batches): review batching threshold config and request size distribution; consider prefix padding in loadgen sample.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep runs reproducible but not brittle: allow small entropy in workload mix when verifying robustness.
- When debugging, shrink steady window to 5m and increase trace sampling to 1:50.
- Prefer resource-isolated VMs for final numbers; k8s E2E introduces scheduling jitter.

Open TODOs
- Add automatic comparison hook that posts diffs to PRs for bench changes (linked to bench-runner PR above).
- Add a small dashboard widget that flags CV outliers automatically.

Appendix: quick commands and example capture recipe
1) Prepare host: sudo systemctl stop bench-agent && sudo sysctl -w vm.drop_caches=3 && export BENCH_IMAGE=sha256:abcd1234
2) Start server with tracing flags: ./serve --model foo.bin --trace-sampler-rate=200 &
3) Start loadgen: bench-runner --config loadgen-config.json --out artifacts/bench-foo.tgz
4) Collect metrics: ./capture-metrics --prometheus http://localhost:9090 --out artifacts/metrics.csv &
5) After steady window, tar artifacts and upload to bench-store with metadata.

If anything in this runbook is unclear, ping @maya in #perf-runs or open ENG-7382 with reproducer and raw artifacts.

End of document
